subject: Logic
title: The Original Position
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Original Position.

hook.text: Before you're born, you pick society's rules—but you don't know if you'll be privileged or disadvantaged.

buildup.text: Rawls's original position extends the veil of ignorance: design all social institutions from behind it.

discovery.text: Rawls argues you'd choose two principles: equal basic liberties, and inequality only if it benefits the worst-off.

twist.text: Libertarians object: why would you prioritize equality over freedom? Utilitarians ask: why not maximize total welfare?

climax.text: The thought experiment doesn't settle the debate—it sharpens it by forcing each side to justify their principles.

punchline.text: Design the rules before you know your place.

quiz.question: What does Rawls's original position require?
options: Knowing your social status in advance
Designing rules without knowing your future position in society
